home.metaDesc: Get started with uptime monitoring, cron job monitoring, alerts, status pages and the REST API.
home.title: Getting started
home.lead: Know when your websites, APIs and scheduled jobs stop working, without running any monitoring servers yourself.
home.w1: Websites and APIs: we request your URL on a schedule and alert you when it fails or the content is wrong. See Monitors.
home.w2: Servers and services: ping a host, check a TCP port or resolve a DNS name.
home.w3: Cron jobs and scheduled tasks: your job pings us when it runs; we alert you when it does not. See Cron job monitoring.
home.hFirst: Set up your first monitor in a minute
home.s1: <registerLink>Create a free account</registerLink> and confirm your email.
home.s2: Open Monitors → New monitor, choose a type and enter the address.
home.s3: Open Notifications and add where alerts should go (email, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, ntfy, Pushover, webhook or SMS). Your account email always receives alerts unless you turn them off.
home.s4: Optional: create a <statusLink>status page</statusLink> so your customers can see the state of your services.
home.callout: Checks run from our infrastructure, separate from yours. If your own server goes down, we still notice.
home.automate: Everything in the dashboard is also available through the <apiLink>REST API</apiLink> (Pro and Business plans), so monitors can be created from your deployment scripts.

monitors.metaDesc: Monitor types, check intervals, advanced settings, maintenance windows and monitor states.
monitors.title: Monitors
monitors.lead: A monitor is one thing you want to keep an eye on: a website, an API endpoint, a server or a scheduled job.

http.name: HTTP(s)
http.what: The URL answers with an accepted status code (2xx by default).

keyword.name: HTTP keyword
keyword.what: As HTTP, and the response body contains your keyword.

port.name: TCP port
port.what: A TCP connection to the port succeeds.

heartbeat.name: Heartbeat
heartbeat.what: Your job pings us on time. See <heartbeatLink>cron job monitoring</heartbeatLink>.
heartbeat.addr: None: we give you a ping URL

monitors.warn: For security, addresses must be reachable from the public internet. Private and internal addresses (localhost, 10.x, 192.168.x, cloud metadata addresses) are rejected. If you enter an address without http:// or https://, https:// is assumed.
monitors.interval: How often we check depends on your plan: slower on Free, faster on Pro and Business. The fastest allowed interval for your plan is shown when you add a monitor.
monitors.down: Down: the last check failed. You are alerted once when a monitor goes down and once when it recovers, not on every failed check.
monitors.paused: Paused: you paused it, or it was paused because your plan limit was lowered. Paused monitors are not checked and send no alerts.
monitors.maint: Maintenance: a scheduled maintenance window is running. No alerts are sent and no incidents are recorded.
monitors.advancedIntro: Open Advanced settings in the monitor form (or edit an existing monitor) to fine-tune how a monitor behaves:
monitors.a1: Retries: how many failed checks in a row before the monitor is marked down. This avoids false alarms from one-off network blips.
monitors.a2: Timeout and retry interval: how long to wait for a response and how quickly to re-check after a failure.
monitors.a3: Accepted status codes and HTTP method: for example accept 200-299 and 301, or check with HEAD. You can also send custom headers (JSON) and a request body.
monitors.a4: Redirects and TLS: follow redirects, ignore TLS errors, and get warned before the SSL certificate expires.
monitors.a5: Upside-down mode: marks the monitor down when the target is reachable, useful to make sure something is not exposed.
monitors.a6: Repeat alert: re-send the down alert every N checks until the monitor recovers.
monitors.a7: Tags and description: group monitors with tags and filter the list by them.
monitors.detail: Each monitor has a detail page with the current response time, the 24-hour average, uptime for 24 hours, 30 days and 1 year, the SSL certificate and domain expiry dates, a response-time chart for 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days, and the incident history. Domain expiry is not published for every domain extension (for example .tr), in which case it shows as unavailable.
monitors.maintenance: Open Maintenance to schedule a window for one or more monitors. While it runs, alerts for those monitors are silenced and no incidents are recorded, so planned work does not look like an outage.
monitors.pause: Use Pause on the list or detail page to stop checks without losing history. Delete removes the monitor and its history permanently.
monitors.limits: Each plan has a maximum number of monitors. If you exceed it after a downgrade, your oldest monitors stay active and the newest are paused, never deleted. See <pricingLink>pricing</pricingLink> for the current limits.

heartbeat.metaDesc: Monitor cron jobs, backups and scheduled tasks with heartbeat pings.
heartbeat.title: Cron job monitoring
heartbeat.lead: Backups, reports and sync jobs fail silently. A heartbeat monitor alerts you when a job does not run on time.
heartbeat.h1: Create a monitor of type Heartbeat (cron job). Choose how often the job should run (the period) and how late it may be (the grace time).
heartbeat.h2: We give you a unique ping URL. Keep it secret: anyone who has it can send pings.
heartbeat.h3: Make your job request that URL every time it succeeds. If no ping arrives within period + grace time, we alert you.
heartbeat.failMeaning: The job failed. You are alerted immediately, without waiting for the deadline.
heartbeat.methods: GET, POST and HEAD are accepted. You can attach a short message with ?msg=backup%20done or in a POST body (first 200 characters). Pings are limited to 120 per minute per monitor.
heartbeat.cronTitle: crontab: ping only when the job succeeds
heartbeat.shellTitle: shell: report success or failure explicitly
heartbeat.c1: Period: how often the job is supposed to run (hourly, daily, weekly).
heartbeat.c2: Grace time: a little more than the longest the job normally takes. If your backup runs for ten minutes, a grace time of 15 to 30 minutes avoids false alarms.
heartbeat.c3: A failed job that never ran at all also triggers the alert once the deadline passes.
heartbeat.callout: Use curl --retry so a short network problem does not cause a missed ping, and set a timeout so a hanging request never blocks your job.
heartbeat.not: Heartbeats prove that a job reported in. They do not check that a website is reachable. For that, add an HTTP monitor as well.

alerts.metaDesc: Where alerts can go and how to set each channel up.
alerts.title: Alerts & integrations
alerts.lead: You get one alert when a monitor goes down and one when it comes back, in the places you already work.
alerts.intro: Your account email always receives alerts unless you turn them off in Settings. Add more places under Notifications. Use Send test after adding a channel to check it works; a successful test marks the channel as verified, and only verified channels receive alerts.
alerts.email: Any address. We send a confirmation link; the channel is active once you confirm.
alerts.slack: An incoming webhook URL (Slack: Apps → Incoming Webhooks).
alerts.discord: A channel webhook URL (Channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks).
alerts.telegram: A bot token from @BotFather and the chat ID (or @channelname) the bot can post to.
alerts.teams: A Workflows or incoming webhook URL for the channel.
alerts.googleChat: A space webhook URL (Space → Apps & integrations → Webhooks).
alerts.ntfy: A topic name. Uses ntfy.sh by default; enter your own server address (and an access token if it requires one) to self-host.
alerts.pushover: Your Pushover user key and an application token.
alerts.webhook: Any public HTTPS endpoint. We send a JSON POST (see below).
alerts.sms: A phone number in international format, e.g. +447700900123.
alerts.warn: Webhook URLs must be public. Private and internal addresses are rejected, and redirects are not followed. Channel secrets such as webhook URLs and bot tokens are stored encrypted.
alerts.maint: During a scheduled maintenance window alerts for the affected monitors are not sent.
alerts.prefs: In Settings you can choose which emails you receive: monitor down, monitor recovered, billing, trial reminders and plan-limit warnings. Account and security emails cannot be turned off.

statusPages.metaDesc: Publish a status page and embed status badges.
statusPages.title: Status pages & badges
statusPages.lead: Show customers how your services are doing, with a 90-day uptime history and incident log.
statusPages.create: Open Status pages → New status page, choose a title, an address and the monitors to show. The page is public and available at your-address.{domain}. Each plan includes a limited number of pages.
statusPages.c1: Each monitor shows its current state, 90-day uptime percentage and a bar per day.
statusPages.c2: Down periods appear in the incident history with start and end times.
statusPages.c3: Paused monitors are shown as paused and do not affect the overall status.
statusPages.domain: On Pro and Business you can serve the page from your own domain, for example status.yourcompany.com:
statusPages.d1: Enter the domain when you create the status page.
statusPages.d2: At your DNS provider, add a CNAME record for that name pointing to cname.{domain} (shown in the form).
statusPages.d3: An SSL certificate is issued automatically the first time the domain is visited. This can take a minute.
statusPages.domainWarn: The certificate is only issued once your DNS points at us. Apex domains (without a subdomain) cannot use a CNAME at most providers; use a subdomain such as status..
statusPages.badges: Embed a live badge for any public status page in a README, dashboard or website. Replace your-address with your status page address.
statusPages.badgesNote: Badges refresh about once a minute and only show information that is already public on your status page.

api.metaDesc: Manage monitors from your own scripts with the REST API.
api.title: REST API
api.lead: Create, list and delete monitors from deployment scripts and CI. Available on Pro and Business plans.
api.auth: Create a key under Dashboard → API. The key is shown once; we store only a hash. Send it as a bearer token:
api.authWarn: Treat keys like passwords. Revoke a key from the same page if it leaks. Keys stop working if the account is downgraded to a plan without API access.
api.base: Requests and responses are JSON. Successful responses wrap the result in data; errors use error.
api.epDelete: Delete a monitor and its history.
api.fType: HTTP, KEYWORD, PING, PORT, DNS or HEARTBEAT. Required.
api.fUrl: Address to check. Not used for HEARTBEAT. PORT uses host:port.
api.fInterval: Seconds between checks (HEARTBEAT: how often the job should run). Limited by your plan.
api.fKeyword: KEYWORD only: text that must appear in the response.
api.fGrace: HEARTBEAT only: seconds a ping may be late. Default 0.
api.pingUrlNote: For HEARTBEAT monitors the response also contains pingUrl, the URL your job should request.
api.e400: Invalid or unsafe input, for example a private address.
api.e401: Missing, invalid or revoked API key.
api.e402: Your plan does not allow this (monitor count, check interval, API access).
api.e404: No such monitor (monitors of other accounts are never visible).
api.e429: Too many requests. Wait for the number of seconds in the Retry-After header.
api.rate: Each API key may make 60 requests per minute. Creating and deleting monitors is also limited to 30 operations per minute per account.
